text:
Riley: hi team, day 1. trying to provision a GKE cluster in europe-west4 but `gcloud container clusters create` errors with an org-policy block. attached billing and project under folders/4567000. any fast tips?
Marta (cloud-onboarding): welcome Riley! paste the error and project id. sometimes folders have allowedRegions constraints.
Riley: error: 
ERROR: (gcloud.container.clusters.create) ResponseError: code=403, message=Project 'proj-riley-01' is blocked from region 'europe-west4' by org policy constraints/compute.allowedRegions
proj id: proj-riley-01
Infra Bot: Org policy guide: https://redwood.internal/governance/policy-requests. To check effective policy: `gcloud org-policies describe constraints/compute.allowedRegions --folder=4567000 --effective`
Carlos (infra): looks like folder 4567000 is locked to us regions for now. we can either request a temporary exception or suggest testing in us-central1. Which do you need?
Riley: need EU to validate latency for a PoC. can we get a short exception (48h)?
Marta (cloud-onboarding): ping @Eve (security) for data-residency approval. include justification: "PoC latency testing only; no customer data; 48h."
Eve (security): allowed if sandbox controls are in place. please ensure project has DLP label `non-prod` and no production secrets. I'll approve a 48h exception once DLP tag is verified.
Riley: how do I set DLP label?
Onboard Helper: Add label via gcloud: `gcloud projects update proj-riley-01 --update-labels=dlp=enforced,env=non-prod` and confirm.
Riley: done. labels set.
Carlos (infra): opened policy ticket POL-2026-424 for 48h exception; added justification. awaiting Eve sign-off.
Eve (security): approved. exception granted for proj-riley-01 for 48h. folder 4567000 now includes europe-west4 for this project only.
Riley: retried and cluster created in europe-west4. thanks all! will delete cluster when done. :thumbsup:
